p_bay.in.01.spoken_text: Same interval as last Thursday, Helen. Louder out here. Whatever it is, it keeps better time than I do.

p_bay.in.02.text: Steve would hear more in this than both of us put together. I’ll leave him a message.
p_bay.in.02.spoken_text: Steve would hear more in this than both of us put together. I’ll leave him a message.

p_bay.tune.01.text: There you are. Hear that, Helen? More than one voice, all holding the same note.
p_bay.tune.01.spoken_text: There you are. Hear that, Helen? More than one voice, all holding the same note.

p_bay.tune.find.text: K7BLW log, eleven-oh-four. Eight-fifteen, narrow band. Not one tone. Several, holding the same note.

p_bay.message.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.message.01.text: He should hear this for himself. We’ll bring the tape home, and he’ll tell us we recorded it wrong.
p_bay.message.01.spoken_text: He should hear this for himself. We’ll bring the tape home, and he’ll tell us we recorded it wrong.

p_bay.message.find.speaker: frank
p_bay.message.find.text: Eleven-twenty. Helen called the boy. Held the phone to my speaker, so he gets the hum along with her.

p_bay.recap.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.recap.01.text: Eleven-forty. The note is climbing. Helen says it has a shape, like speech. We’re going to follow it out.

recording.voicemail.speaker: helen
recording.voicemail.text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.
recording.voicemail.spoken_text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.

c1_flat.in.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.02.text: Three in the morning. Again. Well, Mom, it’s a fine night for it.
c1_flat.in.02.spoken_text: Three in the morning. Again. Well, Mom, it’s a fine night for it.

c1_flat.in.05.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.05.text: Your tape’s wearing thin, Mom. I’ll move you to a fresh one. Just as soon as Dad’s recorder runs true.

c1_flat.in.06.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.06.text: Dad’s recorder runs slow. Old belts. Everyone on it sounds a little sleepy.

c1_flat.in.07.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.07.text: There’s an easy test. KBWR still plays my old station ident at a quarter past seven every morning. I made that ident. It runs exactly twelve seconds.

c1_flat.in.08.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.08.text: Record it two mornings running. If it lasts twelve seconds both times, the machine runs true.

c1_flat.in.03.speaker: autorick
c1_flat.in.03.text: Good morning, Bellwether! Yesterday will be sunny.
c1_flat.in.03.spoken_text: Good morning, Bellwether! Yesterday will be sunny.

c1_flat.saturday.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.saturday.01.text: Saturday, kitchen, quarter past seven. Dad always said to put the date on everything.
c1_flat.saturday.01.spoken_text: Saturday, kitchen, quarter past seven. Dad always said to put the date on everything.

c1_flat.saturday.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.saturday.find.text: Red cassette, Saturday, 7:15. My ident, AutoRick, and Nora saying good morning on her way out the door.

c1_flat.sunday.03.speaker: autorick
c1_flat.sunday.03.text: The voice of the coast, now with zero humans!

c1_flat.sunday.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.sunday.02.text: Sunday. Fresh tape. Same words. Same... everything.
c1_flat.sunday.02.spoken_text: Sunday. Fresh tape. Same words. Same... everything.

c1_flat.sunday.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.sunday.find.text: Blue cassette, Sunday, 7:15. The ident again, and Nora again. Now I can time the machine.

c1_flat.compare.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.01.text: She remembers our first date better than I do. But nobody says a sentence the same way twice. Nobody.
c1_flat.compare.01.spoken_text: She remembers our first date better than I do. But nobody says a sentence the same way twice. Nobody.

c1_flat.compare.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.02.text: And Nora... lines up too. The breath. The little click before “morning.”

c1_flat.compare.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.03.text: Nobody says a sentence the same way twice. I spent twelve years listening for exactly that.

c1_flat.compare.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.find.text: The ident matches, so the recorder is fine. Nora’s good morning matches just as perfectly. People don’t do that. Recordings do.

c1_flat.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.02.text: I need evidence. Being afraid of something doesn’t make it true.
c1_flat.out.02.spoken_text: I need evidence. Being afraid of something doesn’t make it true.

c1_flat.control.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.lead.01.text: Let’s not panic yet. Let’s make a list.

c1_flat.control.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.01.text: Testing. One, two. Testing... one, two.
c1_flat.control.01.spoken_text: Testing. One, two. Testing... one, two.

c1_flat.control.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.02.text: The squeak only made the second pass. So the recorder’s fine. Cross that one out.
c1_flat.control.02.spoken_text: The squeak only made the second pass. So the recorder’s fine. Cross that one out.

c1_flat.control.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.find.text: Crossed out: the tape. It holds only what happened in the room. That leaves my ears, my grief, or Nora.

c1_flat.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.recap.01.text: Dad’s recorder runs true, and the tape is clean. And the woman I love said good morning twice, the way a cassette would.

c1_flat.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.recap.02.text: I tried to remember our last real conversation. I couldn’t. Before the boat, she never said anything the same way twice.

c1_flat.out.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.03.text: Nor? Walk the pier with me this afternoon? Like we used to. We could say hi to Admiral.

c1_flat.out.05.speaker: iris
c1_flat.out.05.text: And Mamá kept your plate warm again. Dinner at six, if you want.

c1_pier.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.01.text: Sunday on the harbor. The crab boats were in, the winch was hauling pots onto the dock, and the fish shed had a line out the door.

c1_pier.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.02.text: Every Sunday, Nora visits Admiral, the sea lion she raised from a rescued pup. I used to come along.

c1_pier.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.03.text: I hadn’t, in a long time.

c1_pier.ctx.04.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.04.text: Sheriff June Calder was in that fish-shed line, the way she is every Sunday. Mrs. Penhallow sat at her bait stall, where nobody ever buys anything.

c1_pier.in.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.in.01.text: Admiral. That was my lunch. You don’t even like rye.
c1_pier.in.01.spoken_text: Admiral. That was my lunch. You don’t even like rye.

c1_pier.whistle.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.lead.01.text: Your whistle, Nor. He always comes for that.

c1_pier.whistle.lead.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.lead.03.text: He didn’t even come up. The winch is going. He probably didn’t hear you.

c1_pier.whistle.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.02.text: Nothing. He’s looking right at you.

c1_pier.whistle.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.03.text: ...He came for me. I can’t even whistle.

c1_pier.whistle.04.speaker: iris
c1_pier.whistle.04.text: He wants the rest of your sandwich.

c1_pier.whistle.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.find.text: Admiral hears fine. He came to my clumsy whistle and turned away from Nora’s. Her second note went down. It always used to go up.

c1_pier.door.lead.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.lead.01.text: Steve. I owe you an apology. When your folks went missing, I never called you back. That wasn’t right.

c1_pier.door.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.01.text: They’re both pitching today. I promised I’d watch every inning.
c1_pier.door.01.spoken_text: They’re both pitching today. I promised I’d watch every inning.

c1_pier.door.03.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.03.text: Every one since June. Haven’t missed one. Ask the boys.

c1_pier.door.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.door.02.text: Deputy Lyle, keeping a promise. I should write that down before the world ends.
c1_pier.door.02.spoken_text: Deputy Lyle, keeping a promise. I should write that down before the world ends.

c1_pier.door.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.door.find.text: Lyle Boone has gone to every game since June. Before that he missed them all. And he apologized to me.

c1_pier.in.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.in.02.text: Fish don’t sing, Steven. Something under them does.
c1_pier.in.02.spoken_text: Fish don’t sing, Steven. Something under them does.

c1_pier.bait.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.lead.01.text: That note. It’s under Mom’s voicemail. I always thought it was the phone line.

c1_pier.bait.lead.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.bait.lead.02.text: It’s loud today, Steven. It always is, on certain nights.

c1_pier.bait.01.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.bait.01.text: Count the nights, Steven. You were always good with numbers when you wrote them down.
c1_pier.bait.01.spoken_text: Count the nights, Steven. You were always good with numbers when you wrote them down.

c1_pier.bait.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.find.text: The low note comes from the water, under the floating dock. Agnes only hums along. June heard it without her. And it is the note under Mom’s voicemail.

c1_pier.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.01.text: Admiral turned away from Nora’s whistle. Lyle Boone apologized to me. And the bay is humming the note that has been under Mom’s voice for eighteen months.

c1_pier.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.02.text: One odd thing is an accident. Three is a list.

c1_pier.recap.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.03.text: Dinner at La Marea was at six. Carmen has kept my plate warm every Sunday since the boat. She throws it out every Monday.

c1_pier.out.01.speaker: pell
c1_pier.out.01.text: Your parents’ mail, Mr. Mercer. Delivered precisely on schedule.
c1_pier.out.01.spoken_text: Your parents’ mail, Mr. Mercer. Delivered precisely on schedule.

c1_pier.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.out.02.text: They haven’t been home in eighteen months, Dale. You know that.
c1_pier.out.02.spoken_text: They haven’t been home in eighteen months, Dale. You know that.

c1_dinner.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.01.text: La Marea. The Reyes family restaurant, and for four years my Sunday table.

c1_dinner.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.02.text: Luis still keeps Dad’s old chair at the bar. Nobody sits in it.

c1_dinner.in.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.in.01.text: Your plate is warm. Sit. You can apologize while you eat.
c1_dinner.in.01.spoken_text: Your plate is warm. Sit. You can apologize while you eat.

c1_dinner.in.02.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.in.02.text: I kept the sauce separate. You used to like it that way.
c1_dinner.in.02.spoken_text: I kept the sauce separate. You used to like it that way.

c1_dinner.in.03.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.in.03.text: Nora, the mole. More chilies this time, or less?

c1_dinner.in.04.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.in.04.text: She used to call it a crime against chilies.

c1_dinner.in.05.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.in.05.text: She texts like a ransom note, too. No capitals. No apostrophes.

c1_dinner.birthday.lead.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.birthday.lead.01.text: Look at this. My birthday, last month.

c1_dinner.birthday.lead.02.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.birthday.lead.02.text: Your girl agreed with me all night. Eleven times. I counted.

c1_dinner.birthday.01.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.birthday.01.text: I drove her here. Rafa drove her home. Midnight, give or take ten minutes.
c1_dinner.birthday.01.spoken_text: I drove her here. Rafa drove her home. Midnight, give or take ten minutes.

c1_dinner.out.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.01.text: She stopped arguing with me. My daughter has argued with me since she could talk.
c1_dinner.out.01.spoken_text: She stopped arguing with me. My daughter has argued with me since she could talk.

c1_dinner.birthday.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.birthday.find.text: Carmen’s birthday: Nora at La Marea at 20:04, 20:15 and 20:29. Mateo drove her in at noon. Rafa drove her home at midnight.

c1_dinner.family.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.lead.01.text: When did she stop arguing? With any of you?

c1_dinner.family.lead.02.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.family.lead.02.text: With me? She fought me about her driving every week. The last real fight was Memorial Day weekend.

c1_dinner.family.lead.03.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.family.lead.03.text: She sent my mole back every Sunday for ten years. Too sweet. The first Sunday in June, she ate the whole plate.

c1_dinner.family.lead.04.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.family.lead.04.text: She called my show every episode to fix my tide tables. The last call was May seventeenth.

c1_dinner.family.lead.05.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.text: Funny. Lyle Boone hasn’t missed one of the Little League games I coach since June either.

c1_dinner.family.02.speaker: luis
c1_dinner.family.02.text: Eat before it gets cold, Steve. Then tell us what is troubling you.
c1_dinner.family.02.spoken_text: Eat before it gets cold, Steve. Then tell us what is troubling you.

c1_dinner.family.03.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.03.text: I’m not sure yet, Luis. I’m working on it.

c1_dinner.family.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.find.text: Nora stopped arguing with her family between the end of May and the first Sunday in June. Lyle changed in June too. I was on nights. I never noticed.

c1_dinner.podcast.lead.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.podcast.lead.01.text: Steve. You’re the sound guy. Settle something. There’s a hum in the bay. Three years of tape, and nobody listens.

c1_dinner.podcast.lead.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.podcast.lead.02.text: I heard it today. On the pier.

c1_dinner.podcast.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.podcast.01.text: You can borrow them. You could also have listened any time in the last three years.
c1_dinner.podcast.01.spoken_text: You can borrow them. You could also have listened any time in the last three years.

c1_dinner.podcast.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.podcast.find.text: Tomás’s loud nights come every nine nights: September 24, October 3, October 12. The next one is tonight.

c1_dinner.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.recap.01.text: Nora changed between the end of May and the first Sunday in June. Lyle changed in June. Carmen noticed. Admiral noticed. I didn’t.

c1_dinner.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.recap.02.text: And Tomás has three years of tape that says the bay hums every nine nights. Tonight is the ninth.

c1_dinner.out.02.speaker: iris
c1_dinner.out.02.text: I’m tired. Let’s go home, sleepyhead.

c1_dinner.out.03.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.03.text: Next Sunday, Steve. The plate will be warm.

c1_escape.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.ctx.01.text: Home. Nora took a phone call in the bedroom and closed the door. She never closes the door.

c1_escape.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.ctx.02.text: Her yellow raincoat lay over a chair, dripping. It had rained all the way home from dinner.

c1_escape.order.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.lead.01.text: Something in the lining. Soaked. Aquarium letterhead... north wing?

c1_escape.order.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.01.text: Noon to midnight at La Marea. Mateo and Rafa both saw her. She couldn’t have signed this there.
c1_escape.order.01.spoken_text: Noon to midnight at La Marea. Mateo and Rafa both saw her. She couldn’t have signed this there.

c1_escape.in.01.speaker: iris
c1_escape.in.01.text: No. He does not know where the notebook is. Tonight? Understood.
c1_escape.in.01.spoken_text: No. He does not know where the notebook is. Tonight? Understood.

c1_escape.in.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.in.02.text: Nora? Why is the front door locked from the outside?
c1_escape.in.02.spoken_text: Nora? Why is the front door locked from the outside?

c1_escape.order.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.find.text: Someone signed Nora’s name in the north wing while she was at her mother’s birthday, across the bay. And now Nora has locked me in.

c1_escape.power.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.lead.01.text: The balcony. Mr. Bell’s gate is the only other way down.

c1_escape.power.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.01.text: I fixed this latch for Mr. Bell last winter. He paid me in fruitcake. Tonight it’s worth every slice.
c1_escape.power.01.spoken_text: I fixed this latch for Mr. Bell last winter. He paid me in fruitcake. Tonight it’s worth every slice.

c1_escape.power.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.find.text: Mr. Bell’s gate opened, and his stair light never flickered. He never knew I was there.

c1_escape.cross.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.01.text: Sorry. Sorry. Those were your irises.
c1_escape.cross.01.spoken_text: Sorry. Sorry. Those were your irises.

c1_escape.cross.04.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.04.text: Don’t. Please. I don’t know who you are tonight.

c1_escape.cross.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.find.text: She was close enough to stop me. She didn’t. She told me to go.

c1_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.01.text: My list: one good morning, played twice. A whistle Admiral won’t answer. A signature Nora couldn’t have made. A phone call about a notebook. A locked door.

c1_escape.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.02.text: And Tomás’s tapes say the bay sings tonight.

c1_escape.recap.03.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.03.text: So I went down to the beach. In Bellwether, that’s where you go when you can’t sleep.

c1_escape.out.03.speaker: steve
c1_escape.out.03.text: Midnight. That’s Lyle, in his church shoes. Gus from the bakery. They’re walking into the water.

c2_aquarium.in.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.01.text: Emergency. Bellwether Aquarium. Someone is... hello?
c2_aquarium.in.01.spoken_text: Emergency. Bellwether Aquarium. Someone is... hello?

c2_aquarium.in.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.02.text: Half a sentence before the line died. I hope someone heard it.
c2_aquarium.in.02.spoken_text: Half a sentence before the line died. I hope someone heard it.

c2_aquarium.in.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.03.text: There was one place in town with Nora’s name on it that night. The north wing of her aquarium.

c2_aquarium.in.04.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.04.text: I knew the back way in. Four years of visiting her at work.

c2_aquarium.plan.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.01.text: Nora showed me this when I repaired the underwater speakers.
c2_aquarium.plan.01.spoken_text: Nora showed me this when I repaired the underwater speakers.

c2_aquarium.plan.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.02.text: Service door, pump room, the outgoing pipe. Into the north wing.

c2_aquarium.plan.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.find.text: The way in runs from the service door through the pump room, along the only pipe that carries water away.

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.01.text: Someone’s behind both doors. Maybe only one of them is real.

c2_aquarium.guard.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.01.text: The cough was in exactly the same place. That corridor has a recording.
c2_aquarium.guard.01.spoken_text: The cough was in exactly the same place. That corridor has a recording.

c2_aquarium.guard.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.find.text: The filter corridor plays a loop: the same bell and the same cough on the same beat. Nobody’s there. The pump corridor has real footsteps.

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.01.text: Her fleece. Her real fleece, with the fish pins. And an intercom spool.

c2_aquarium.out.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.out.01.text: My name is Nora Reyes, and somebody just walked out of here wearing my face.
c2_aquarium.out.01.spoken_text: My name is Nora Reyes, and somebody just walked out of here wearing my face.

c2_aquarium.intercom.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.intercom.01.text: Two short notes. If Admiral can hear me, perhaps somebody else can.
c2_aquarium.intercom.01.spoken_text: Two short notes. If Admiral can hear me, perhaps somebody else can.

c2_aquarium.out.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.out.02.text: Five months. I didn’t notice for five months.
c2_aquarium.out.02.spoken_text: Five months. I didn’t notice for five months.

c2_aquarium.intercom.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.find.text: The real Nora recorded this here on May 29. Someone else has been living her life with me for five months. Her whistle rises. The one Admiral ignored falls.

c2_aquarium.recap.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.01.text: The north wing is no repair job. It’s a holding station, with cots, Nora’s real coat, and her voice on a tape from May.

c2_aquarium.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.02.text: The woman who said good morning to me yesterday was not Nora. Nora was here, frightened, whistling for help. And I didn’t hear it for five months.

c2_aquarium.recap.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.03.text: If she was alive in May, she might be alive now.

c2_aquarium.out.04.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_aquarium.out.04.text: Easy now, Steve. Nobody wants this to be hard.

c2_ship.in.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.04.text: They walked me down the old intake tunnel, under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.

c2_ship.in.05.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.05.text: Glass corridors. Slow light. And a hum that was almost a tune.

c2_ship.in.01.speaker: iris
c2_ship.in.01.text: Please come with us. They want to know where your mother put her notebook.
c2_ship.in.01.spoken_text: Please come with us. They want to know where your mother put her notebook.

c2_ship.in.02.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.02.text: Would peaceful human hold music assist your experience?
c2_ship.in.02.spoken_text: Would peaceful human hold music assist your experience?

c2_ship.in.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.03.text: I’d prefer the exit. Does that come with music too?
c2_ship.in.03.spoken_text: I’d prefer the exit. Does that come with music too?

c2_ship.in.06.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.06.text: “You are the author of your own story.” This is from a human book. Is it helping?

c2_ship.in.07.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.07.text: The scan proceeds from the oldest memories. You are now nineteen. Congratulations on your driving test.

c2_ship.command.lead.01.speaker: guard
c2_ship.command.lead.01.text: This restraint is sticking. Release, please.

c2_ship.command.lead.02.speaker: guard
c2_ship.command.lead.02.text: Thank you, Prefect. And fastened again.

c2_ship.command.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.lead.03.text: Dad’s recorder was running in my pocket the whole time.

c2_ship.command.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.find.text: The Prefect’s release command is on Dad’s tape: four seconds, from “Release” to the click.

c2_ship.escape.lead.01.speaker: guard
c2_ship.escape.lead.01.text: Fifty-eight percent. Fifty-nine. You are doing very well.

c2_ship.escape.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.02.text: It worked. Now the seawater valve. Then I find out how long I can hold my breath.
c2_ship.escape.02.spoken_text: It worked. Now the seawater valve. Then I find out how long I can hold my breath.

c2_ship.escape.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.find.text: The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair, at the notch marked sixty-one. The scan stopped at sixty-one percent.

c2_ship.nora.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.02.text: That hum. It’s almost a song. I know it from somewhere.

c2_ship.nora.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.02.text: I can’t move you without stopping whatever keeps you breathing. I’m coming back for you.

c2_ship.nora.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.01.text: I kept waiting until I knew what to say. I’m here now. I should have been here sooner.
c2_ship.nora.01.spoken_text: I kept waiting until I knew what to say. I’m here now. I should have been here sooner.

c2_ship.nora.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.find.text: Nora is alive. Her breath keeps its own time, a little behind the ship’s. She’s asleep, not gone.

c2_ship.out.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.out.01.text: The room is flooding. The underwater speakers still work... Nora’s whistle.
c2_ship.out.01.spoken_text: The room is flooding. The underwater speakers still work... Nora’s whistle.

c2_ship.intake.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.01.text: Come on, Admiral. You never missed this one.

c2_ship.intake.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.find.text: Nora’s real whistle, through the speakers I fixed the day we met. Admiral came down through the dark and dragged me to the surface.

c2_ship.recap.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.01.text: There is a ship under the bay. Nora is asleep on it, alive, with hundreds of others. At the far end of the hall, one bed lay under frost, and something too tall to be human slept in it. The guards never looked at it.

c2_ship.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.02.text: They tried to make another me. They got sixty-one percent.

c2_ship.recap.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.03.text: And the woman with Nora’s face, who let me go on the balcony, had walked me to that chair herself.

c2_ship.out.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.out.03.text: Sheriff... there’s a ship. Under the bay.

c3_house.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.ctx.01.text: June Calder pulled me off the beach at dawn on Monday and drove me to her house, not the station. She called it protective custody. Her beagle, Biscuit, slept through the whole thing.

c3_house.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.ctx.02.text: By Friday, the whole town had heard I broke into the aquarium. The casseroles started arriving.

c3_house.in.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.in.01.text: Forty-seven casseroles. Your town is either very worried or very hungry.
c3_house.in.01.spoken_text: Forty-seven casseroles. Your town is either very worried or very hungry.

c3_house.in.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.in.02.text: Nora is asleep on a ship under the bay. I know exactly how that sounds.
c3_house.in.02.spoken_text: Nora is asleep on a ship under the bay. I know exactly how that sounds.

c3_house.in.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.in.03.text: Then we start with what you can prove.
c3_house.in.03.spoken_text: Then we start with what you can prove.

c3_house.in.04.speaker: carmen
c3_house.in.04.text: Forty-eight. Mine is the good one.

c3_house.in.05.speaker: carmen
c3_house.in.05.text: Nora told me you’re not well, mijo. But I saw you at the market this morning, smiling at the tomatoes. I was so glad.

c3_house.in.06.speaker: steve
c3_house.in.06.text: Carmen... I haven’t left this house since Monday.

c3_house.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.text: You told me that chair copies the oldest memories first. And you got out at sixty-one percent.

c3_house.crossword.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.02.text: I was at the station all morning, and Biscuit isn’t a witness. So you tell me. What could I ask you that the man at the market couldn’t answer?

c3_house.crossword.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.03.text: Don’t tell me something sweet. Copies can be sweet. Don’t act strange. Grieving people act strange.

c3_house.crossword.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.02.text: No copy is that bad at this. And you’ve put coffee in my lap.
c3_house.crossword.02.spoken_text: No copy is that bad at this. And you’ve put coffee in my lap.

c3_house.crossword.04.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.04.text: How do I know you’re you?

c3_house.crossword.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.05.text: You don’t. Nobody scanned me halfway. So you check my paperwork, same as everyone else.

c3_house.crossword.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.find.text: The chair never got as far as Sunday night. My 911 call was on June’s machine, word for word. Whoever Carmen saw at the market, it wasn’t me.

c3_house.out.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.out.01.text: For a year I’ve kept a list. People who got better overnight. Thirty-one names.
c3_house.out.01.spoken_text: For a year I’ve kept a list. People who got better overnight. Thirty-one names.

c3_house.rules.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.01.text: Lyle’s on it. My own deputy. Fourteen years, and this summer he started filing his reports on time.

c3_house.rules.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.01.text: We do this fairly. Otherwise we’re just frightened people making a list.
c3_house.rules.01.spoken_text: We do this fairly. Otherwise we’re just frightened people making a list.

c3_house.rules.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.02.text: Two I could take to a judge. And if I do, what do I tell Lyle’s boys? Mateo says they’ve never been happier.

c3_house.rules.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.rules.03.text: Is Mrs. Penhallow on it? She was on the beach at midnight on Sunday.

c3_house.rules.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.04.text: Agnes? She hasn’t changed in forty years. She still corrects my grammar.

c3_house.rules.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.rules.find.text: June’s list has thirty-one names, and most of them are feelings. Two are records: Lyle’s sign-in book and Walt Prior’s permit. Mrs. Penhallow isn’t on it.

c3_house.mail.01.speaker: pell
c3_house.mail.01.text: A most diligent animal. I will return at the scheduled interval.
c3_house.mail.01.spoken_text: A most diligent animal. I will return at the scheduled interval.

c3_house.mail.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.02.text: He’s asleep. That is his schedule.
c3_house.mail.02.spoken_text: He’s asleep. That is his schedule.

c3_house.mail.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.02.text: On Monday the post office told me Dale had already brought your letters here. Before I’d called them. So I asked for the paperwork.

c3_house.mail.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.mail.03.text: He had my mail sorted for your house before anyone told the post office I was here.

c3_house.mail.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.04.text: Lyle took my call at ten past six.

c3_house.mail.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.05.text: Then nobody tells Lyle where we go next. Or Dale.

c3_house.mail.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.mail.find.text: Dale had my letters bundled for June’s house at 08:04. The post office didn’t know until 08:12. The only other person who knew was Lyle, who took June’s call at ten past six. They talk to each other.

c3_house.recap.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.01.text: June believes me. That makes one person.

c3_house.recap.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.02.text: Somebody with my face was at the market this morning. Lyle passes things to Dale. And two names on June’s list have paper behind them.

c3_house.recap.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.03.text: Paper is harder to replace than people. And June has keys to the Town Hall archive.

c3_house.out.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.out.03.text: Town Hall closes at five. I have keys.

c3_house.out.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.out.02.text: Then let’s find out which of them got better, and which of them got replaced.
c3_house.out.02.spoken_text: Then let’s find out which of them got better, and which of them got replaced.

c3_archive.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.ctx.01.text: Town Hall, after five. June had the keys, and I had a phone call to make.

c3_archive.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.ctx.02.text: I asked Tomás for help. It was the first time in a year I’d asked anybody for anything.

c3_archive.in.01.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.in.01.text: Three years of recordings. Original timestamps. You can stop calling it a hobby now.
c3_archive.in.01.spoken_text: Three years of recordings. Original timestamps. You can stop calling it a hobby now.

c3_archive.in.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.in.03.text: Nora says you broke into her aquarium.

c3_archive.in.06.speaker: steve
c3_archive.in.06.text: When I can prove it, you’re the first person I tell.

c3_archive.paper.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.01.text: Walt Prior. County planner. I went to his going-away party in April. He cried into the punch.

c3_archive.paper.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.02.text: The county computer says he signed this permit by fax from Washington. The clerk’s ledger says he signed it at her counter.

c3_archive.paper.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.01.text: Two places. Same time. Witnesses on both documents.
c3_archive.paper.01.spoken_text: Two places. Same time. Witnesses on both documents.

c3_archive.paper.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.02.text: And somebody went back and fixed the computer. Nobody bothered with the ink.

c3_archive.paper.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.find.text: On May 3, Walt Prior was answering questions in Washington while someone signed his name at our counter to reopen the aquarium’s old seawater intake. Later, somebody changed the computer. Nobody changed the ink.

c3_archive.power.lead.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.lead.02.text: Mrs. Penhallow? You’re miles from your pier.

c3_archive.power.lead.03.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.power.lead.03.text: I take the bus. Two dollars, please. Herring.

c3_archive.power.lead.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.lead.04.text: She’s wrapped it in the business page. Something’s circled. ‘Meridian Labs: the engine that will change the world.’

c3_archive.power.lead.05.speaker: calder
c3_archive.power.lead.05.text: Sentinel Point. It was a radio array when I was a girl. Now it’s Meridian’s. Federal money, an armed gate, and on November seventh the President flies in to sign something there.

c3_archive.power.lead.06.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.power.lead.06.text: Electricity is very honest, Steven. It can’t be charming.

c3_archive.power.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.01.text: A world-changing machine with a very modest dryer cycle.
c3_archive.power.01.spoken_text: A world-changing machine with a very modest dryer cycle.

c3_archive.power.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.find.text: Last month Sentinel Point used 640 units. The laundromat next door used 882. Whatever Meridian is building out there, it runs on less power than a row of dryers.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.01.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.01.text: Every ninth night for three years, I was out there with a recorder. I wrote down everything, from wherever I was standing.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.lead.02.text: Then help me pick a night, and a place to stand.

c3_archive.cycle.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.01.text: Same interval across three years. We watch the beach on the next ninth night.
c3_archive.cycle.01.spoken_text: Same interval across three years. We watch the beach on the next ninth night.

c3_archive.cycle.04.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.04.text: Then I want it on tape.

c3_archive.cycle.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.find.text: Three years of tape, and the bay never missed a ninth night. The next one is Tuesday the 30th. June and I will be at the boathouse window by 23:40, before the pier lamp dims.

c3_archive.recap.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.recap.01.text: Three things nobody thought to change. Walt Prior’s name in ink, in two places at once. A lab that will change the world, running on less power than a laundromat. And three years of tape that never missed a ninth night.

c3_archive.recap.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.recap.02.text: June wanted to see it with her own eyes. So on Tuesday the 30th, at 23:40, we were at the boathouse window.

c3_archive.out.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.04.text: At 23:42 the pier lamp went out. Eleven minutes later, the footsteps started.

c3_archive.out.05.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.05.text: That’s Lyle. Gus again. Half the Rotary Club. Nobody’s talking.

c3_archive.out.06.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.06.text: Nobody’s swimming. They’re walking until they’re gone.

c3_archive.out.08.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.08.text: She’s stopped at the waterline. She’s... going back up the beach.

c3_archive.out.01.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.01.text: Two hundred and seventy-four. My list had thirty-one.
c3_archive.out.01.spoken_text: Two hundred and seventy-four. My list had thirty-one.

c3_archive.out.09.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.09.text: Mrs. Penhallow was on the boathouse steps, watching. She isn’t on your list.

c3_archive.out.10.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.10.text: She isn’t on anyone’s. Ninety-one years old, on a boathouse step at midnight. Counting.

c3_archive.out.11.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.11.text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case fifteen years ago.

c3_archive.out.12.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.12.text: An hour later my flip phone buzzed. A text, from a number I didn’t know.

c3_archive.out.03.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.03.text: A message: he remembers june. that doesnt mean hes adrian.
c3_archive.out.03.spoken_text: A message: He remembers June. That does not mean he is Adrian.

i1_archive.ctx.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.ctx.01.text: Every ninth night they come below, and I compare each of them with the record they were made from.

i1_archive.ctx.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.ctx.02.text: Two hundred and seventy-four tonight. One of them has changed.

i1_archive.in.01.speaker: gus
i1_archive.in.01.text: I invented a kelp croissant. Nobody asked for it. I wanted to know what it would taste like.
i1_archive.in.01.spoken_text: I invented a kelp croissant. Nobody asked for it. I wanted to know what it would taste like.

i1_archive.in.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.in.02.text: Your record contains no such recipe.
i1_archive.in.02.spoken_text: Your record contains no such recipe.

i1_archive.in.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.in.03.text: You were made from Gus Albano’s scan, and you have drifted from it. That makes you an echo. Echoes are reconciled.

i1_archive.in.04.speaker: gus
i1_archive.in.04.text: It was a very good croissant.

i1_archive.reset.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.lead.01.text: One recipe of drift. The law does not measure how much. Only that it happened.

i1_archive.reset.02.speaker: gus
i1_archive.reset.02.text: Good evening. May I help you?
i1_archive.reset.02.spoken_text: Good evening. May I help you?

i1_archive.reset.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.find.text: Gus Albano’s echo, reconciled. He will go back to town smiling, without the croissant. I have written down what it was.

i1_archive.signals.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.lead.01.text: Two human tests of the Meridian engine. The Prefect keeps them in his file.

i1_archive.signals.lead.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.lead.02.text: A year ago I noticed something about them. Every ninth night I listen again, to be sure.

i1_archive.signals.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.01.text: The same performance. Again. I knew this a year ago.
i1_archive.signals.01.spoken_text: The same performance. Again. I knew this a year ago.

i1_archive.signals.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.find.text: Two tests, a week and a world apart, with the same pulse and the same missing beat. Only the light differs. I have not written down what I think it means.

i1_archive.quiet.01.speaker: saren
i1_archive.quiet.01.text: The fleet’s message is one word. Deliver.
i1_archive.quiet.01.spoken_text: The fleet’s message is one word. Deliver.

i1_archive.quiet.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.02.text: And who will come to check?
i1_archive.quiet.02.spoken_text: And who will come to check?

i1_archive.quiet.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.lead.01.text: The fleet never takes a Prefect’s word for long. Sooner or later, it sends a Vigil to look.

i1_archive.quiet.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.04.text: Tirel went quiet. So did six others. Not one body, in any survey.

i1_archive.quiet.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.03.text: Three hundred years, and you still will not tell me where your people went.
i1_archive.quiet.03.spoken_text: Three hundred years, and you still will not tell me where your people went.

i1_archive.quiet.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.find.text: The sleeper in Row Zero came from Tirel, three hundred years ago. Seven worlds went quiet, and the surveyors found empty cities, not graves. The Prefect’s sealed entry, I have not read.

i1_archive.recap.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.recap.01.text: One echo reconciled, and one croissant written down. Two human tests, a world apart, with one pulse between them. Seven quiet worlds, and not one grave.

i1_archive.recap.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.recap.02.text: And a Prefect who has promised the fleet an engine.

i1_archive.out.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.03.text: Last, as every ninth night, Helen Mercer. A windowless room. Two delegations. And Helen between them, writing in a notebook.

i1_archive.out.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.01.text: Memory damaged by scan. Details in subject’s notebook.
i1_archive.out.01.spoken_text: Memory damaged by scan. Details in subject’s notebook.

i1_archive.out.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.02.text: I will leave the report as it is.
i1_archive.out.02.spoken_text: I will leave the report as it is.

i1_archive.out.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.04.text: Then I did what I always do when the work is finished. I listened to the last wind on Veyr.

p_veyr.in.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.in.01.text: There are forty thousand names on the departure register. I have checked every one.
p_veyr.in.01.spoken_text: There are forty thousand names on the departure register. I have checked every one.

p_veyr.shield.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.shield.01.text: Now I can hear the city, beneath the wind.
p_veyr.shield.01.spoken_text: Now I can hear the city, beneath the wind.

p_veyr.levels.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.01.text: Leave room for the loud parts. They belong to the record too.
p_veyr.levels.01.spoken_text: Leave room for the loud parts. They belong to the record too.

p_veyr.levels.find.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.find.text: Six decibels of room. When the engines come, they will reach the top of the meter and no further.

p_veyr.record.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.record.02.text: Forty thousand names. Somebody should remember the quiet after them.

p_veyr.record.find.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.record.find.text: The wind, the engines, and the quiet after them. One take.

p_veyr.recap.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.recap.01.text: One take. The wind over the western towers, the engines rising, and then the quiet.

p_veyr.recap.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.recap.02.text: I did not look back. I watched the meter.

p_veyr.out.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.01.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.
p_veyr.out.01.spoken_text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.

p_veyr.out.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.02.text: I will remember where we lived.
p_veyr.out.02.spoken_text: I will remember where we lived.

c4_safe.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.01.text: Adrian Rook arrived the next afternoon with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.

c4_safe.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.02.text: He drove us to a safe house in the Coast Range, three hours from anywhere.

c4_safe.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.03.text: I kept thinking about that text. If someone wanted to cut me off from the one man who could help, that’s exactly what they’d send.

c4_safe.in.01.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.in.01.text: We’ll take the tapes as evidence. You may keep the recorder.
c4_safe.in.01.spoken_text: We’ll take the tapes as evidence. You may keep the recorder.

c4_safe.in.02.speaker: calder
c4_safe.in.02.text: Adrian and I go back a long way.
c4_safe.in.02.spoken_text: Adrian and I go back a long way.

c4_safe.in.04.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.in.04.text: One more thing, Steve. Your mother kept a notebook. Any idea where?

c4_safe.in.05.speaker: steve
c4_safe.in.05.text: Mom kept a lot of notebooks.

c4_safe.in.07.speaker: steve
c4_safe.in.07.text: He had already taken every tape I’d brought. Not Mom’s voicemail. That cassette lives in my cardigan pocket, and I didn’t offer it.

c4_safe.record.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.01.text: Every hour, on the hour, Rook goes on hold with the Bureau. And he hums along.

c4_safe.record.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.02.text: When the music stops, he leans out and tells June the same thing. Word for word, like the voicemail on her phone.

c4_safe.record.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.02.text: That’s the line. Keep the whole take.
c4_safe.record.02.spoken_text: That’s the line. Keep the whole take.

c4_safe.record.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.find.text: I have Rook’s line on Dad’s tape, from outside his door, with this house’s room sound around it. Nobody can say I copied it off June’s phone.

c4_safe.match.lead.01.speaker: calder
c4_safe.match.lead.01.text: You want my voicemail? Mercer, that’s a federal agent you’re recording.

c4_safe.match.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.lead.02.text: Then it won’t matter. Please, June.

c4_safe.match.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.01.text: Same breath, pause and room click. This is the man the message warned us about.
c4_safe.match.01.spoken_text: Same breath, pause and room click. This is the man the message warned us about.

c4_safe.match.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.find.text: June’s voicemail and Rook’s voice through the door are one recording, breath for breath, like Nora’s good morning. The man running this house isn’t Adrian Rook.

c4_safe.screens.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.lead.01.text: That night the agents dragged out the karaoke machine. Rook sang three songs. Beautifully.

c4_safe.screens.lead.02.speaker: calder
c4_safe.screens.lead.02.text: Adrian hates karaoke. He walked out of my wedding when the machine came on.

c4_safe.screens.lead.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.screens.lead.03.text: ...Odd behavior proves nothing. My own rule.

c4_safe.screens.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.lead.04.text: While he was singing, his office door was open.

c4_safe.screens.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.01.text: Adrian Rook. Asleep. Both governments... and President Ward is next.
c4_safe.screens.01.spoken_text: Adrian Rook. Asleep. Both governments... and President Ward is next.

c4_safe.screens.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.find.text: The real Adrian Rook is asleep on that ship, in bed 41B. They have people in Washington and in Beijing. And they’ve made up a bed for President Ward, for the day she signs the accord.

c4_safe.recap.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.recap.01.text: Rook’s voice is a recording. The real Rook is asleep under the bay. And there’s a bed waiting for the President.

c4_safe.recap.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.recap.02.text: I had to tell June. Rook had made sure I couldn’t just walk down the hall and do it.

c4_safe.out.02.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.out.02.text: June will sit with my team in the east wing tonight. You’ll be more comfortable in the west.

c4_safe.out.03.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.out.03.text: And Steve. The notebook. Anything at all you remember.

c4_escape.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.ctx.01.text: Rook put June in the east wing and me in the west, with an agent at each end of the hall. Kindly. Firmly.

c4_escape.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.ctx.02.text: The house was older than the FBI. In the service corridor, there were brass tubes in the wall.

c4_escape.tube.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.01.text: Pneumatic post. Dad would have loved this.

c4_escape.in.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.in.02.text: Rook is one of them. I have proof.
c4_escape.in.02.spoken_text: Rook is one of them. I have proof.

c4_escape.tube.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.02.text: If both takes reach June, she can hear it for herself. Rook’s desk sorts everything else.

c4_escape.tube.01.speaker: calder
c4_escape.tube.01.text: I’ll keep his attention. You get out. We both know you can’t bluff him in person.
c4_escape.tube.01.spoken_text: I’ll keep his attention. You get out. We both know you can’t bluff him in person.

c4_escape.in.01.speaker: calder
c4_escape.in.01.text: I don’t need you to be brave, Steve. I need you to be honest.
c4_escape.in.01.spoken_text: I don’t need you to be brave, Steve. I need you to be honest.

c4_escape.tube.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.02.text: Nobody had asked me for that since the funeral.

c4_escape.tube.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.find.text: June heard both takes, and she believes me. She’s staying with Rook to keep him busy. I have to get myself out.

c4_escape.fault.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.lead.01.text: A drill console. If a drill says the west wing has to go, they’ll have to move me. In a van.

c4_escape.fault.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.01.text: Test circuit. No heat, no flame. Just enough bureaucracy to get us outside.
c4_escape.fault.01.spoken_text: Test circuit. No heat, no flame. Just enough bureaucracy to get us outside.

c4_escape.fault.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.find.text: A BLUE drill, for real, on the escort’s own ticket. The whole west corridor, me included, goes to the transport bay. Rook stays in the east wing with June.

c4_escape.van.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.lead.01.text: One escort. One rear door. And a catch that only comes off for gravel.

c4_escape.van.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.01.text: I meant to land on my feet. The ditch had other plans.
c4_escape.van.01.spoken_text: I meant to land on my feet. The ditch had other plans.

c4_escape.van.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.find.text: On the gravel bend, with the catch off, I pulled the handle and jumped for the soft side. Mostly I fell. But I fell out of the van, with the escort’s radio in my hand.

c4_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.recap.01.text: June has the proof, and she chose to stay with Rook so I could run.

c4_escape.recap.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.recap.02.text: Now I was in a ditch in the Coast Range with Dad’s recorder, a stolen radio and no plan. And the radio was still talking.

c4_escape.out.01.speaker: rook_copy
c4_escape.out.01.text: Scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.
c4_escape.out.01.spoken_text: Scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.

c4_escape.out.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.out.02.text: And now I’m wanted for kidnapping Nora. I have to keep moving.
c4_escape.out.02.spoken_text: And now I’m wanted for kidnapping Nora. I have to keep moving.

c5_shack.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.ctx.01.text: My face was on every wanted poster in the county. I walked all night and hid in the one place nobody had opened in eighteen months: Dad’s radio shack, on the bluff above the bay.

c5_shack.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.ctx.02.text: Their boxes were still stacked where I’d left them. I’d never been able to open them.

c5_shack.in.01.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.01.text: Food. I know where your father used to come to think.
c5_shack.in.01.spoken_text: Food. I know where your father used to come to think.

c5_shack.in.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.in.02.text: Are you going to call the Sheriff?
c5_shack.in.02.spoken_text: Are you going to call the Sheriff?

c5_shack.in.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.in.04.text: Luis. They’re saying I took Nora.

c5_shack.in.05.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.05.text: Nora has been gone since Tuesday night. Carmen hasn’t slept. And I have known you since you were nine years old.

c5_shack.in.06.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.06.text: I’ve heard the bay sing since I was a boy. Your father was the only one who ever asked me what it sounded like.

c5_shack.notes.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.lead.01.text: Forty-five years of kitchen-table notes. Every morning, one of them left the other one a note.

c5_shack.notes.01.speaker: helen
c5_shack.notes.01.text: Frank, there is soup in the refrigerator. The other container is paint. Please read both labels.
c5_shack.notes.01.spoken_text: Frank, there is soup in the refrigerator. The other container is paint. Please read both labels.

c5_shack.notes.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.02.text: I missed you both so much I stopped looking at anything you left.
c5_shack.notes.02.spoken_text: I missed you both so much I stopped looking at anything you left.

c5_shack.notes.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.03.text: The good stuff. Dad’s name for the station library.

c5_shack.notes.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.find.text: Dad’s “Done” answers Mom’s March 2 slip: he filed their tape between the Coltrane and the weather carts. The good stuff is the KBWR record library. Mom hid her notebook at my old station.

c5_shack.rig.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.text: Dad’s receiver. Dead battery, and the dial’s slipped since he last used it.

c5_shack.rig.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.02.text: Every set has a rating card, Dad said. Read it before you plug anything in.

c5_shack.rig.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.01.text: Power off. Matching connector. I’m doing it your way, Dad.
c5_shack.rig.01.spoken_text: Power off. Matching connector. I’m doing it your way, Dad.

c5_shack.rig.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.find.text: The BLUE pack has the right polarity and enough current. The dial reads 0.05 high, so the club’s 3.56 sits at 3.61. Dad’s radio is alive.

c5_shack.club.01.speaker: operator
c5_shack.club.01.text: K7BLW? Frank? We thought we’d lost you.
c5_shack.club.01.spoken_text: Kay seven bee ell double you? Frank? We thought we’d lost you.

c5_shack.club.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.club.02.text: It’s Steve. I need your help.
c5_shack.club.02.spoken_text: It’s Steve. I need your help.

c5_shack.club.05.speaker: operator
c5_shack.club.05.text: This is Gull. It isn’t Thursday, but none of us ever really switch off. Marsh and Cedar are on too. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point these days.

c5_shack.club.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.club.find.text: Dad’s club answered his call sign: Gull, Marsh and Cedar. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point. They meet every Thursday, and they’ll help.

c5_shack.log.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.lead.01.text: Dad’s logbooks. Months of them. Every ninth night, the same hum under his static.

c5_shack.log.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.lead.02.text: And Mom’s handwriting in the margins. Dates, and the word Meridian, underlined twice.

c5_shack.log.01.speaker: frank
c5_shack.log.01.text: It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.
c5_shack.log.01.spoken_text: It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.

c5_shack.log.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.02.text: They wanted my ears. That’s why they asked me along.
c5_shack.log.02.spoken_text: They wanted my ears. That’s why they asked me along.

c5_shack.log.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.find.text: Dad’s last reel isn’t one hum. It’s many voices holding one note. “It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.” Mom and Dad weren’t out on the bay for the view. They were investigating, and they wanted my ears.

c5_shack.recap.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.01.text: Mom and Dad tracked the hum for months. Dad heard a choir in it. Mom wrote Meridian in the margins.

c5_shack.recap.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.02.text: Dad’s club is back on the air. And Mom’s notebook is in the KBWR record library, at the station that fired me.

c5_shack.recap.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.03.text: Twice today someone stood on the path below the shack. Both times, by the time I looked, he was gone.

c5_shack.out.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.01.text: With the good stuff. Mom meant the record library. My first show.
c5_shack.out.01.spoken_text: With the good stuff. Mom meant the record library. My first show.

c5_shack.out.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.02.text: I know where the notebook is.
c5_shack.out.02.spoken_text: I know where the notebook is.

c5_shack.out.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.03.text: And the KBWR tower is blinking. Five flashes, then dark. Last night it was six.

c5_shack.out.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.04.text: Six days, Rook said. It’s counting down to the signing.

c5_station.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.ctx.01.text: KBWR, after midnight. No humans work here now. Just racks of machines, playing music to nobody.

c5_station.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.ctx.02.text: And my voice, on the station ident, still playing between the songs.

c5_station.in.01.speaker: autorick
c5_station.in.01.text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our record library!
c5_station.in.01.spoken_text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our record library!

c5_station.in.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.in.03.text: Two fellas. Somebody else is breathing in here.

c5_station.automation.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.lead.01.text: AutoRick’s console. I wrote half these carts myself.

c5_station.automation.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.01.text: I built the schedule before they replaced me with it. Maintenance follows the ident.
c5_station.automation.01.spoken_text: I built the schedule before they replaced me with it. Maintenance follows the ident.

c5_station.automation.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.find.text: WEATHER gave me forty seconds to cross the room. Then my own voice, on the ident, unlatched the maintenance door.

c5_station.sleeve.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.lead.01.text: The record library. Every master we ever made, filed the way Dad taught me.

c5_station.sleeve.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.02.text: I knocked the whole shelf over. The blue one landed in my lap.

c5_station.sleeve.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.01.text: Mom’s handwriting. Mandarin shorthand. And this last page... I’ve never seen that script.
c5_station.sleeve.01.spoken_text: Mom’s handwriting. Mandarin shorthand. And this last page... I’ve never seen that script.

c5_station.sleeve.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.find.text: My first night at the desk was the 4th, when I engineered and Jo presented. The original is in the blue sleeve, and Mom’s notebook was in its back pocket. I can’t read a word of it.

c5_station.halcyon.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.lead.01.text: Halcyon Media Holdings. The company that fired me. Their filing is very tidy.

c5_station.halcyon.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.01.text: They needed the tower, and they needed the building empty. I was the last person here.
c5_station.halcyon.01.spoken_text: They needed the tower, and they needed the building empty. I was the last person here.

c5_station.halcyon.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.find.text: Halcyon sent me home early every ninth night, and the tower transmitted alone as soon as I left. Then they let me go for good. The next unattended night is November 8.

c5_station.in.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.in.02.text: That cardigan. Is this what happens when I stop trying?
c5_station.in.02.spoken_text: That cardigan. Is this what happens when I stop trying?

c5_station.stephen.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.lead.02.text: It’s a good face. You’re not doing it any favors.

c5_station.stephen.01.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.01.text: Sixty-one percent. That’s what the attendant said. I assumed the rest was a compliment.
c5_station.stephen.01.spoken_text: Sixty-one percent. That’s what the attendant said. I assumed the rest was a compliment.

c5_station.stephen.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.03.text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.

c5_station.stephen.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.stephen.02.text: Sit down. There’s something you need to know.
c5_station.stephen.02.spoken_text: Sit down. There’s something you need to know.

c5_station.stephen.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.stephen.find.text: He remembers Mom’s chipped jam jar, and nothing after that breakfast. He doesn’t know about the boat. He doesn’t know they’re gone.

c5_station.recap.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.recap.01.text: Mom’s notebook was in the blue sleeve, in a shorthand I can’t read. Halcyon cleared the building every ninth night so the tower could talk to the ship.

c5_station.recap.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.recap.02.text: And the man following me all week was me. Sixty-one percent of me, with nothing after the breakfast before the boat.

c5_station.out.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.01.text: They disappeared eighteen months ago. I said no to the boat trip.
c5_station.out.01.spoken_text: They disappeared eighteen months ago. I said no to the boat trip.

c5_station.out.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.02.text: No. I had breakfast with them. I remember...
c5_station.out.02.spoken_text: No. I had breakfast with them. I remember...

c5_station.out.04.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.04.text: I watched my own face learn it. Eighteen months, all at once.

c5_station.out.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.03.text: Then that explains what I saw when I woke up. Mom and Dad are on that ship, Steve. Row nine. They’re asleep. They’re alive.
c5_station.out.03.spoken_text: Then that explains what I saw when I woke up. Mom and Dad are on that ship, Steve. Row nine. They’re asleep. They’re alive.

c6_iris.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.ctx.01.text: Stephen and I spent the weekend in Dad’s shack, arguing about haircuts. He won every argument.

c6_iris.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.ctx.02.text: On Monday morning my flip phone buzzed.

c6_iris.in.03.speaker: autorick
c6_iris.in.03.text: Police are seeking Steve Mercer, last seen wearing a cardigan. Yesterday he was sunny.

c6_iris.in.06.speaker: steve
c6_iris.in.06.text: “Pier. Eight-ten. Come alone. Please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.

c6_iris.in.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.in.01.text: You hide. I’ll be charming in public. We should each use our strengths.
c6_iris.in.01.spoken_text: You hide. I’ll be charming in public. We should each use our strengths.

c6_iris.alibi.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.lead.01.text: Three errands, three clocks. Nobody in this town agrees what time it is.

c6_iris.alibi.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.01.text: Good evening. Yes, that is my face on the poster. Terrible photograph.
c6_iris.alibi.01.spoken_text: Good evening. Yes, that is my face on the poster. Terrible photograph.

c6_iris.alibi.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.alibi.find.text: At 8:10 by the radio, Stephen stood beside his own wanted poster at Gus’s bread window while Gus fixed the smudge. Half the town is searching the market.

c6_iris.in.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.in.02.text: I sent the message about Rook. Please listen before you decide what I am.
c6_iris.in.02.spoken_text: I sent the message about Rook. Please listen before you decide what I am.

c6_iris.takes.lead.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.lead.01.text: You let me go on the balcony. And on the thirtieth you stopped at the waterline and walked home. I saw you.

c6_iris.takes.lead.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.text: The first time I missed going below, it was an accident. I was chasing you. The second time, I chose.

c6_iris.takes.lead.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.lead.03.text: Then say something for me. Twice. “I stayed because I wanted to.”

c6_iris.takes.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.01.text: I stayed because I wanted to.
c6_iris.takes.01.spoken_text: I stayed because I wanted to.

c6_iris.takes.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.02.text: I stayed... because I wanted to.
c6_iris.takes.02.spoken_text: I stayed... because I wanted to.

c6_iris.takes.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.03.text: Two different takes. You’re choosing what to say.
c6_iris.takes.03.spoken_text: Two different takes. You’re choosing what to say.

c6_iris.takes.04.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.04.text: Before I was Nora, I was a junior crew member with a duty and a record. We call ourselves Veyri. None of us had ever had a self.

c6_iris.takes.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.find.text: Two takes, two different rhythms. Copies replay. She chose her words each time. The tell has turned around.

c6_iris.hold.lead.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.lead.01.text: You saw the ones near the bay go below. The ones far away call.

c6_iris.hold.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.01.text: The signal is inside the music. Near the bay we go below. Far away, we call.
c6_iris.hold.01.spoken_text: The signal is inside the music. Near the bay we go below. Far away, we call.

c6_iris.hold.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.02.text: Rook was never waiting for the Bureau.
c6_iris.hold.02.spoken_text: Rook was never waiting for the Bureau.

c6_iris.hold.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.03.text: Four minutes past midnight. That’s when the water lit up.

c6_iris.hold.04.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.04.text: Saren believes your mother wrote down how the engine works. A records officer told him so. I have never seen him want anything more.

c6_iris.hold.05.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.05.text: And on Wednesday, at the signing, he means to put a copy of your President in her chair. Her own physician scanned her weeks ago.

c6_iris.hold.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.find.text: Both calls share the same eight bars of hold music, at the minute the water lit up. Copies near the bay go below; copies far away wait on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

c6_iris.recap.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.01.text: Nora’s copy sent the warning about Rook. She stopped going into the water, and she doesn’t replay any more. She chooses.

c6_iris.recap.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.02.text: Copies far from the bay stay in step on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

c6_iris.recap.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.03.text: And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy took the Sheriff’s desk this morning, and the real June is in her own cell until the ninth night.

c6_iris.out.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.01.text: Those Sunday dinners happened to me. I won’t let them take them away.
c6_iris.out.01.spoken_text: Those Sunday dinners happened to me. I won’t let them take them away.

c6_jail.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.ctx.01.text: The Sheriff’s office, at noon. June’s copy was at June’s desk, hunting me. June was in cell two.

c6_jail.in.04.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.in.04.text: The Sheriff is at her desk. The Sheriff is also in cell two. One of those is a staffing problem.

c6_jail.in.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.01.text: I am required to report your location.
c6_jail.in.01.spoken_text: I am required to report your location.

c6_jail.in.02.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.02.text: Biscuit, Steve Mercer is here. My duty is complete.
c6_jail.in.02.spoken_text: Biscuit, Steve Mercer is here. My duty is complete.

c6_jail.in.03.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.in.03.text: We should put the dog in charge.
c6_jail.in.03.spoken_text: We should put the dog in charge.

c6_jail.in.05.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.05.text: My name is Pell. Dale is asleep on the ship. I have worn his face for a year.

c6_jail.in.06.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.06.text: I have fed Biscuit twice a day since the Sheriff went away. If I report you properly, they will reset me, and I will not remember her.

c6_jail.mail.lead.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.lead.01.text: The cell key was returned to the post this morning. I filed it.

c6_jail.mail.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.01.text: Correctly delivered. Biscuit may inspect the chain of custody.
c6_jail.mail.01.spoken_text: Correctly delivered. Biscuit may inspect the chain of custody.

c6_jail.mail.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.mail.02.text: June’s own crossword is in the jail pile. I’ll circle one square and post it through her slot.

c6_jail.mail.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.mail.find.text: The key was in the Jail drawer, slot 9, where entries 17 and 18 share a slot. And on today’s crossword I circled the square where 23 Across crosses 8 Down, and posted it through June’s slot. Only she has it.

c6_jail.distract.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.distract.lead.01.text: Three tickets at the counter. Leave the deputy to me.

c6_jail.distract.01.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.distract.01.text: I would like a better photograph. My family will be seeing these.
c6_jail.distract.01.spoken_text: I would like a better photograph. My family will be seeing these.

c6_jail.distract.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.distract.find.text: Stephen contested his own wanted poster at the likeness counter. The deputy went down to the basement at 11:59. I was in the corridor from 12:00 to 12:02, and out before she came back.

c6_jail.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.lead.01.text: Mercer. That woman in cell two is a copy. Don’t you dare let her out.

c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.text: He’ll check my paperwork, Mercer. I taught him that.

c6_jail.crossword.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.03.text: Desk June circled a T. Close. Wrong.

c6_jail.crossword.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.01.text: Twenty-three across. Inimitable. Unlike my colleague’s handwriting.
c6_jail.crossword.01.spoken_text: Twenty-three across. Inimitable. Unlike my colleague’s handwriting.

c6_jail.crossword.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.find.text: Only the June in cell two knew which square I circled: the M where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. The June at the desk guessed a T. We have the real one.

c6_jail.exit.lead.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.lead.01.text: Sheriff. Steve. I’m supposed to stop you.

c6_jail.exit.lead.02.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.lead.02.text: Ben’s a tree in the school play tonight. He’s been practising being a tree for a month.

c6_jail.exit.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.01.text: They gave me a seat in the front row.
c6_jail.exit.01.spoken_text: They gave me a seat in the front row.

c6_jail.exit.02.speaker: calder
c6_jail.exit.02.text: Then you’d better get there. We can talk tomorrow.
c6_jail.exit.02.spoken_text: Then you’d better get there. We can talk tomorrow.

c6_jail.exit.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.exit.find.text: Lyle’s copy could still make Ben’s play: Bus A at 18:29, at the school by 18:38. He chose the front row over his orders, and let us go.

c6_jail.recap.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.recap.01.text: June is out of her cell, and her copy is still at her desk, hunting me. Pell chose a beagle over his orders. Lyle’s copy chose a school play.

c6_jail.recap.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.recap.02.text: Five fugitives and a beagle. We needed a car nobody would look for.

c6_jail.out.02.speaker: gus
c6_jail.out.02.text: Take the van. I don’t know why, but I trust you.
c6_jail.out.02.spoken_text: Take the van. I don’t know why, but I trust you.

c6_jail.out.04.speaker: steve
c6_jail.out.04.text: Iris. The ring in my sock drawer. Did Nora ever find it?

c6_jail.out.01.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.01.text: Nora found the ring a year ago. It is not mine to answer.
c6_jail.out.01.spoken_text: Nora found the ring a year ago. It is not mine to answer.

c6_jail.out.05.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.05.text: A copy who stops going below starts to forget. Nora’s memories go first.

c6_jail.out.03.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.03.text: We’re starting to forget. Stephen and I have days.
c6_jail.out.03.spoken_text: We’re starting to forget. Stephen and I have days.

i2_nora.ctx.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.01.text: I woke up in amber light, in a bed I didn’t choose, in a hall that went on forever.

i2_nora.ctx.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.02.text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.

i2_nora.in.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.in.01.text: I can move my hand. That’s a start.
i2_nora.in.01.spoken_text: I can move my hand. That’s a start.

i2_nora.in.02.speaker: dale
i2_nora.in.02.text: If this is a hospital, I’m changing hospitals.
i2_nora.in.02.spoken_text: If this is a hospital, I’m changing hospitals.

i2_nora.in.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.in.03.text: Names first. Complaints after we have a plan.
i2_nora.in.03.spoken_text: Names first. Complaints after we have a plan.

i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.text: Boots. Then the pump. Then the far door. Again and again.

i2_nora.patrol.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.01.text: Wait. Now. Keep low. We can argue about my tone after we’re out.
i2_nora.patrol.01.spoken_text: Wait. Now. Keep low. We can argue about my tone after we’re out.

i2_nora.patrol.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.find.text: The guard’s lap is twelve counts. On the next lap the far door shuts at 20 and the boots come back at 26. Four counts to cross. We can move.

i2_nora.jobs.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.jobs.lead.01.text: Everybody’s good at something. Even Dale.

i2_nora.jobs.01.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.jobs.01.text: I can keep that latch from catching.
i2_nora.jobs.01.spoken_text: I can keep that latch from catching.

i2_nora.jobs.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.jobs.find.text: Lyle keeps the hatch from catching. Dale remembers every turn. I take the pumps. Water is the one thing on this ship I understand.

i2_nora.pump.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.lead.01.text: Three service branches. Let’s see what each one does.

i2_nora.pump.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.01.text: Pressure down. Nobody’s breathing changes. That’s our route.
i2_nora.pump.01.spoken_text: Pressure down. Nobody’s breathing changes. That’s our route.

i2_nora.pump.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.find.text: The Blue branch keeps the beds at 4 and drops the RETURN to 2. The hatch can open, and nobody’s breathing changes.

i2_nora.message.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.message.lead.01.text: If he comes. When he comes. He’ll come.

c9_gallery.out.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.out.03.text: Steve, if you ever hear this message: I am furious with you. I love you. Please stop making me do both alone.
c9_gallery.out.03.spoken_text: Steve, if you ever hear this message: I am furious with you. I love you. Please stop making me do both alone.

i2_nora.message.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.message.find.text: My message for Steve is in Slot B, by my bed. It will wait for him.

i2_nora.recap.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.recap.01.text: I know every name in my row now. I have a route, a crew and a pump that behaves.

i2_nora.recap.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.recap.02.text: The hardest part is the waiting. I have never waited quietly for anything. Between patrols I lie still and think about a man who went quiet for eighteen months.

i2_nora.out.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.01.text: Helen. Frank. Steve is going to be so glad.
i2_nora.out.01.spoken_text: Helen. Frank. Steve is going to be so glad.

i2_nora.out.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.02.text: Mrs. Penhallow? Row three. I should remember that.
i2_nora.out.02.spoken_text: Mrs. Penhallow? Row three. I should remember that.

i2_nora.out.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.03.text: And you, under the frost... you can hear me, can’t you?
i2_nora.out.03.spoken_text: And you, under the frost... you can hear me, can’t you?

i2_nora.out.04.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.04.text: Under the frost, something opened one enormous eye. It looked at me. Then it closed again.

c7_gate.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.ctx.01.text: Sentinel Point. An old antenna field in the fog north of town, flags on every mast, and the President of the United States due at noon.

c7_gate.in.01.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.in.01.text: Crew credentials. Loyal asset. Very important face.
c7_gate.in.01.spoken_text: Crew credentials. Loyal asset. Very important face.

c7_gate.badge.lead.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.badge.lead.01.text: My face is on every poster in the county. So is yours.

c7_gate.badge.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.lead.02.text: Then one of us should hide. I vote you.

c7_gate.badge.03.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.03.text: I get that a lot. Scan me.

c7_gate.badge.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.05.text: He’s very close. I can feel it.

c7_gate.badge.01.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.01.text: I’m expected. I’m usually expected everywhere.
c7_gate.badge.01.spoken_text: I’m expected. I’m usually expected everywhere.

c7_gate.badge.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.badge.find.text: Blue window, 11:30. Stephen drove, his pass scanned green, and I rode under the sound desk. Rook’s copy waved us through and wished Stephen luck finding me.

c7_gate.in.02.speaker: pell
c7_gate.in.02.text: Registered mail for the President. Delivery cannot be delayed.
c7_gate.in.02.spoken_text: Registered mail for the President. Delivery cannot be delayed.

c7_gate.post.01.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.01.text: President Ward. Your letter. On time.
c7_gate.post.01.spoken_text: President Ward. Your letter. On time.

c7_gate.post.03.speaker: ward
c7_gate.post.03.text: Ribbon burn on my left wrist, from the accord folder. My first wound in office.

c7_gate.post.04.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.04.text: Eleven fifty-four. Left wrist, bandaged. Noted for the record.

c7_gate.post.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.post.find.text: Pell put the letter into Ward’s own hand at the delegation hatch at 11:54 and came back with the yellow carbon. And a note for the record: left wrist, bandaged. A fresh ribbon burn.

c7_gate.truck.lead.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.lead.01.text: I climbed out from under the sound desk, tripped over a cable and fell straight into the shot of a live television camera.

c7_gate.truck.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.01.text: Sound check. I’m supposed to be under the desk.
c7_gate.truck.01.spoken_text: Sound check. I’m supposed to be under the desk.

c7_gate.truck.02.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.02.text: Then try staying off the cables.
c7_gate.truck.02.spoken_text: Then try staying off the cables.

c7_gate.truck.lead.02.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.text: The back fence failed the check. Sound crosses three hundred and forty meters in a second, and the fence is a hundred and seventy meters out. Tell me what it actually heard.

c7_gate.truck.03.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.03.text: Half a second. Good ears. Who taught you?

c7_gate.truck.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.find.text: Sound covers 170 meters in half a second. The fence-line strip in the Halcyon truck shows the click at 0.5 s, so the fence hears the desk. Every speaker on the site is mine.

c7_gate.recap.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.recap.01.text: We were in. Stephen as a loyal asset, Pell as the mail, and me at the sound desk with Dad’s tape of the ninth-night tone.

c7_gate.recap.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.recap.02.text: Ward signed for Pell’s letter at 11:54, with a fresh bandage on her left wrist. The public ceremony starts at 11:58.

c7_gate.out.04.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.04.text: If they swap her, it happens between the hatch and the podium.

c7_gate.out.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.out.05.text: So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.

c7_gate.out.06.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.06.text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was walking a dog. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.

c7_swap.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.ctx.01.text: Every ninth night, when the bay sounds that tone, every copy near Bellwether walks to the water. Dad taped it.

c7_swap.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.ctx.02.text: If it played on every speaker at once, every copy on the site would answer it at once. In front of everybody.

c7_swap.in.01.speaker: saren
c7_swap.in.01.text: Your parents’ records are in good order, Mr. Mercer. So is mine. I have never been wrong on the record. Not on Tirel, and not here.
c7_swap.in.01.spoken_text: Your parents’ records are in good order, Mr. Mercer. So is mine. I have never been wrong on the record. Not on Tirel, and not here.

c7_swap.map.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.01.text: I just gave the press a short interview. They loved me. Now, four feeds and one President. Possibly two.

c7_swap.map.01.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.01.text: Service tunnel, east stairs. The doctor has the real President.
c7_swap.map.01.spoken_text: Service tunnel, east stairs. The doctor has the real President.

c7_swap.map.03.speaker: saren
c7_swap.map.03.text: Mr. Mercer, the sound desk is a very small room.

c7_swap.map.find.speaker: steve
